Evaluations of the following energy carriers are included in this study: sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) (biomass-based and power-to- liquids [PtL]), cryogenic hydrogen (LH ), liquefied natural gas (LNG), liquefied ethane (LE), 2 and Jet X. Some motivations for producing and consuming alternative aviation fuels are U.S. dependence on imported crude oil to supply domestic refineries, as well as to address the expected forward- year growth in demand for jet fuel. Petroleum refineries produce gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, and other fuels and chemicals. A reduction in demand for gasoline and diesel could negatively impact jet fuel supply. In 2025, the United States consumed 27 billion gallons of Jet A, representing approximately 27% of world consumption (EIA 2025d, 2025e, IATA 2025b). Unlike gasoline and diesel, Jet A consumption continues to increase, illustrating the need for solutions to increase domestic fuel production and reduce aircraft emissions (EIA 2025d).
